title: LQ Watchtower: proactive latency-vs-quality probe for batching & cache heuristic changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Recent configuration churn in batching shapes and KV-cache heuristics has produced hard-to-predict latency vs. quality tradeoffs across slices of traffic. Existing regression alerts are either too coarse (global LQ deltas) or too noisy (per-slice flapping). We need a targeted, automated probe that quantifies the LQ impact of a config change at canary and rollout time and gates auto-rollouts when regressions exceed defined tolerances.

Goal: Implement the 'LQ Watchtower' probe — an automated evaluation and monitoring artifact that runs before/during/after config/model changes to produce a compact risk score (stability score) and human-readable diagnostics for engineers: 1) per-slice latency percentile uplift (p50/p95/p99), 2) quality regressions (turn-level accuracy + token-level perplexity proxies + contrast-set answers), 3) blended risk metric for rollout gating. Integrate probe output into Console rollouts and alerting.

Why this is different: Rather than only sampling aggregate LQ metrics, Watchtower focuses on delta-driven probes that synthesize synthetic prefixes, edge-case slices, and production-sampled requests to measure how a change shifts the latency-quality frontier for representative workloads. It provides deterministic probes that can run in CI, canary, and post-rollout audits.
acceptance_criteria: A Watchtower probe binary/proc that can be triggered with a config change (CLI + REST) and completes within 30 minutes for standard probe profiles

Probe outputs a JSON summary with: stability_score (0-100), per-slice latency deltas (p50/p95/p99), per-slice quality deltas (turn-level f1/accuracy, token-level perplexity proxy), and a ranked list of top 5 examples where quality regressed
Probe integrates with Console rollout UI: shown as a step in canary that blocks automated rollout when stability_score < 75
Alerting rule created in PagerDuty/Monitoring: severity threshold for stability_score < 60 and high-risk slice detection (>= 3 slices with >=5% quality drop AND >=10% p95 latency increase)
Unit and integration tests covering synthetic-prefix generation, slice-weighted aggregation, and stable reproduction of a known regression (fixture), with CI gating
Playbook documented in Confluence with troubleshooting steps, links to synthetic datasets, and rollback thresholds
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Probe spec and harness (3d): define probe profiles (lite, standard, heavy), slice taxonomy, and required metrics; author synthetic prefix generator and contrast-set sampler

Phase 2 - Local harness + CI integration (5d): implement probe runner (Python) that can call runtime with config overrides; add unit tests and CI job to run 'standard' profile on PRs touching batching/kvcache code
Phase 3 - Canary integration (4d): wire probe into canary pipeline so it runs against canary traffic snapshot and publishes JSON summary to Console storage
Phase 4 - Alerting & rollout gate (2d): add stability_score evaluation in rollout policies and configure monitoring alerts; draft PD escalation path
Phase 5 - Post-rollout audit job (1d): scheduled daily probe to detect drift/regressions introduced by config flips; emit weekly report
metrics_and_measurements: Latency: p50, p95, p99 delta (ms) per slice
Quality: turn-level accuracy / rubric F1; token-level perplexity proxy (log-loss on token predictions); contrast-set pass rate
Stability_score: weighted combination of normalized latency and quality deltas (explainable formula) between 0-100
False-positive guard: minimum sample size per slice = 200 requests
Time budget: standard profile must finish within 30 minutes; lite within 5 minutes
monitoring_and_alerting: Console: add Watchtower step artifact visible in rollout timeline with JSON download and human summary
Monitoring: new stability_score metric exported to metrics system (timeseries) tagged by change_id, config_hash, model_version
Alert: stability_score < 60 triggers P1 to oncall; stability_score [60-75) triggers P2 review
Dashboard: per-change latency-quality frontier visualizer and top-regressed-example viewer
On-call playbook: quick rollback command, how to interpret top-5 regressed examples, thresholds to approve rollout
risk: Probe sampling bias: synthetic prefixes may not correlate with all production slices — mitigate by including production-sampled reservoir and slice-weighed aggregation
Time-to-run: heavy profile could delay rollouts — default to 'standard' in automated flows and run 'heavy' manually
Metric misalignment: stability_score relies on normalization that could overweight latency for some customers — expose tuning knobs per-tenant in dedicated flows
Data privacy: production-sampled examples must be scrubbed of PII before storing or showing in Console
rollback_and_gating: Automatic block when stability_score < 75 during canary with at least 10% of traffic sampled
Manual override requires owner approval and documented risk justification in rollout notes
Rollback steps documented with CLI commands and expected downtime/impact
Fallback policy: if probe errors out, conservative default is to block automated rollout and require manual review
